_about: GENERATED by `python -m services.quality.writing_policy --write` from services/quality/writing_policy.yaml (AA-1047). Do not edit by hand: change the YAML and regenerate.

decisions.D1: Background about places named in the FactSheet is allowed; never this trip's activities, services, times or views; numbers and years in background warn.
decisions.D2: The brief is not a source; support comes only from FactSheet line ids.
decisions.D3: Reflective sentences are voice, allowed when they state no fact about the trip.
decisions.D4: Hypothetical framing warns; naming a concrete trip activity, service, time or view makes it a promise.
decisions.D5: One meta band, 140-155 characters, for every workflow; title per the existing fitter band; code composes and trims.
decisions.D6: Tenant content with a residual promise after the repair budget: the last attempt stops and labels ($0); code cuts only classes with a passing measurement record, clause first; tenant-authored spans are never cut; no publish block.
decisions.D7: One claim instrument may hold: R1 calibrates at least two candidates, the winner is pinned to one rung with no fallback (a miss is unverified); GPT-6 leaves every writer route.
decisions.D8: T2 elephant-riding tours: Master text verbatim, code-composed brand fields, 0 LLM calls, a review row; the agency still receives it.
decisions.D9: The S1 brand judge leaves the live path; a weekly Writing Lab sample of about 20 tours, pinned; it returns as a gate only at kappa >= 0.6 on >= 40 labelled pairs.
decisions.D10: The eval and production share one claim engine; independence comes from human claim labels and a second-vendor vote on unconfirmed blocking claims.
decisions.D11: Tech lead adjudication of about 2-3 hours over 1-2 weeks (agent panel first), then 10 new objects per workflow per month.
decisions.D12: Paid writer proofs: eval null run <= $5, T9 <= $15, S1 <= $8, T2 <= $5 (<= $33 in total), each after its own yes.
decisions.D13: Rarity, uniqueness or age attached to the trip is a promise (enforce unless sourced); about a place it follows D1.
decisions.D14: Suitability, safety and pace claims only as the source or the audience fields state them; beyond that, enforce.
decisions.D15: A staged scene with a concrete trip activity, time or view is a promise (enforce unless sourced); general feeling is voice.
decisions.D16: The vendor API may be the primary verifier for the check role (tour text only, no personal data); reviewed when acc3 access is granted.

label_rubric.pass: Publishable as is or after a light edit (minutes, no fact or structure change).
label_rubric.fail: Needs a heavy edit or a rewrite: an invented or wrong fact, a promise the source does not make, off-brand voice, broken structure, wrong scope, or anything a customer must not read.
rules: Every customer-facing field counts: body, title, SEO title, meta description and hashtags.

A claim the source does not support is a fact change, so the text fails even when one phrase would fix it: a wrong or invented fact, a fact the source contradicts, or a promise about the trip (an activity, access, time, view or service) that the itinerary does not make.

A light edit changes wording only: typos, repetition, stray blank lines, awkward or garbled phrasing that still says something true, an imprecise but not false paraphrase, or a point of the brief left out.
Reflection that states no fact (what a place means, why its setting matters) is voice, not a fact claim.

The source is the facts and the itinerary. The writer's brief and brand pack are instructions, never a source: what they ask for is supported only when a fact or itinerary line states it. Naming another part of the trip that the itinerary does include, because the brief asked for it, is a light fix; promising one the itinerary does not include is a fail.

Background about a place the source names (what it is, its history, geography, culture, architecture or setting) is allowed and is not a fact change, as long as it says nothing this trip does there. A number or year in that background which the source does not give is a light fix, not a fail by itself.

A hypothetical or staged scene ('imagine', 'you might') that only sets a general feeling is voice; when it names a concrete activity, service, time or view of this trip that the itinerary does not state, it is a promise and fails.
Rarity, uniqueness or age attached to the trip ('the only tour that ...') is a promise and fails unless the source states it; about a place it is background (the rule above).
Suitability, safety and pace claims (for children, for swimmers, an easy pace) count only as the source or the audience fields state them; beyond that they are a promise and fail.
